Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking our RFP questions. We are trying to map the incremental sync behavior to our existing ETL windows and need a concrete handshake/fallback plan for the migration. Specifically we need:
- A step-by-step sequence for an incremental sync cutover (initial snapshot, incremental catch-up, switchover).
- Expected downtime or degradation risk per step (if any).
- Canary strategy: traffic split approach, sample size, validation gates.
- Fallback and rollback procedures (how to revert without data loss).
- Pre-warm / cache-warm recommendations and how long warmup takes at 1TB dataset scale.
- Data drift detection and post-cutover validation suite (what tests you run).
- Security controls during migration (who has DB access, audit logs).

We have two weekend maintenance windows we can give you (Dec 18–19 or Jan 8–9). Can you send a proposed timeline and indicate what information you need from our infra team?

Attachments: Interchange-RFP-questions.pdf (pdf)

Tara Singh

Hi Tara — thanks for the clear list. We put together a draft sequence and initial timeline that aligns with a two-week prep + canary + cutover pattern; sending as an attachment for your review. High-level notes:

- Week 0 (prep): schema mapping, access windows, test corpus, and acceptance criteria sign-off.
- Week 1 (snapshot & initial catch-up): initial bulk transfer outside business hours; validation run.
- Week 2 (incremental replay & warmup): continuous incremental sync, KV/prefix cache warm-up (we expect warm cache benefits after ~30–90 minutes at 1TB depending on distribution).
- Canary (2–3 days): 5–10% traffic to Redwood runtime with automated validation gates (latency, token fidelity, sample prompt set).
- Cutover day: increase traffic to 50% → monitor 4 hours → full switch if gates pass.
- Fallback: automatic routing back to existing endpoints; we retain prefetched prefix state for 48 hours to minimize repeat work.

Questions for Interchange before we lock dates:
1) Can your infra provide read-only DB replicas during the snapshot?
2) Which teams are authorized for emergency rollback (names + emails)?
3) Will you accept our suggested test prompt set (we included examples in the draft)?

I attached "incremental-sync-draft.xlsx" with a GANTT and owner map. If Dec 18–19 is available we can aim for a decoupled canary starting Dec 11 for perf validation.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP: Incremental sync handshake + fallback schedule (technical notes)

Couple of technical clarifications / proposals for the draft:

- Snapshot approach: use a logical export (export job -> object store) rather than a block-level copy to avoid schema drift. We recommend 2-phase validation: row-count + hash spot-checks.
- Incremental ingestion: CDC stream (Kafka / Kinesis) with idempotent consumers on our side. We keep an ingestion watermark; if watermark gap > threshold we trigger a catch-up snapshot.
- Canary routing: traffic split at the L7 edge with header flagging. Start at 5% -> 15% -> 50% as gates pass. Each step has a 4-hour hold window.
- Cache warm: prefix cache should be warmed using a synthetic keyset from your top-1000 prompt templates; plan for a 45–75 minute warm window at our expected QPS.
- Rollback: two mechanisms — soft-fail routing to your legacy endpoint (automated) + DB-level transaction window to replay deltas if needed. Soft-fail keeps existing service online and collects logs for postmortem.

I can produce a short-runbook (scripts + smoke-tests) for the canary. Priyom — please weigh in on the DB access/privilege steps and runtime throttles we should include.

- Aditya

- Runbook items: preflight checklist (DB credentials rotated for the snapshot job), canary playbook (who executes traffic shift), and post-cutover verification checklist (rolling hashes + sanity queries).
